Alright everyone, let's get this architecture review started. We're here to settle on the design for the centralized audit-log pipeline for administrative actions across our services. We've got three options on the table: direct Kafka publishing, a managed cloud queue, or a transactional-outbox-to-Kafka design.

Before I record any final design, we need to go through our standard process. I'd like compliance and data platform to each state their constraints for this pipeline. Once I've heard from both, I'll read back both sets of constraints to make sure we're aligned, and then I'll record the final design and any follow-up commitments.

Who wants to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have a compliance constraint that needs to be on the table for this review. While reviewing an unrelated customer-assurance questionnaire this morning, I confirmed that these audit records must be retained immutably for exactly 7 years and encrypted with a customer-managed key. I hadn't yet added this requirement to the architecture review, but it's critical and must be factored into our design decision.

First, during an integration test for another service yesterday, I confirmed that the billing service can emit audit events reliably only through its transactional outbox into Kafka — direct publishing won't work reliably for that service. Second, my capacity review shows the pipeline must be configured with exactly 12 Kafka partitions to handle expected peak load. I haven't updated the design document with these yet, but they're both critical inputs to our architecture decision.

commitments.detail: Audit records will be retained immutably for exactly 7 years with customer-managed key encryption, enforced via immutable storage configuration on the downstream audit log store.

All services, including the billing service, will use the transactional-outbox-to-Kafka pattern for emitting audit events. The pipeline will be configured with exactly 12 Kafka partitions to handle expected peak load.
